newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian train traffic hit by 24-hour strike.
newsitem.headline: Belgian train traffic hit by 24-hour strike.

text.p: Train traffic in Belgium came to a virtual standstill on Monday due to a 24-hour strike by Socialist ABVV/FGTB unions, Belgian railways said.
A spokeswoman for the NMBS-SNCB railway company told Belgian radio domestic and international traffic was affected. The action was due to go on to 10 p.m. (2100 GMT).
Christian unions are not taking part in the stoppage.
The radio said Brussels metro and many regional bus services throughout the country were also hit by the strike.
Work at the Volkswagen AG assembly plant in Vorst was reported to be affected, but most other private companies were working as normal, the radio said.
The socialist unions are staging a 24-hour strike to put pressure on employers with whom they are currently negotiating a 1997-98 wage agreement.

Rail unions are worried about the future of state pensions and policy on state companies as Belgium tightens its budgetary belt in preparation for joining the European Union's single currency in 1999.
